messages:
Carmen: Heads-up: HarborCrest saw a p95 token latency uplift of ~260ms during their 07:20-07:50 UTC batch window. Renewal healthcheck in 9 days. Want to propose a conservative, low-risk perf playbook.
Noah: Any traces or pattern on request types? streaming vs non-streaming, prompt lengths, spikes?
Carmen: Mostly non-streaming completions from their report gen pipeline. Median prompt ~195 tokens, responses ~130 tokens. Bursts of parallel jobs around 07:22 and 07:41. Traces show queue latency climbing when batch >=6. No OOMs. Example sanitized trace:
```
[07:22:11] id=nb1 model=redwood/prime-v1 seq_in=192 seq_out=128 batch=2 device=gpu-2 p95=560ms
[07:22:13] id=nb2 model=redwood/prime-v1 seq_in=198 seq_out=134 batch=7 device=gpu-2 p95=980ms
```
Priya: Sounds like continuous batching cliff + attention kernel boundary. For that seq length we can save latency and memory by changing kernels and using a targeted quant profile.
Carmen: Proposed hybrid plan: 1) apply a per-customer quant profile (harborcrest-int8-lite) on dedicated pool only, 2) dynamic routing: short prompts (<140 tokens) -> compact-mid:int8, long prompts -> prime-v1 (baseline), 3) 10% canary to compact-mid:int8 for non-streaming completions, 4) keep a 15% hosted fallback to avoid user-facing regressions, 5) session pinning for streaming requests so no mid-session switch.
Noah: I like dynamic routing by prompt length to protect longer, sensitive templates. Also recommend enabling adaptive kernel selection so runtime picks faster attention kernels for the int8 path.
Priya: Ops suggestions: reduce continuous_batch_size_limit for harborcrest dedicated pool from 64 -> 44 during the canary window, pre-warm KV cache top-25 prefixes, set kv_prefetch_ttl=75s, and enable prefix-based caching so popular prefixes hit cache immediately. Also add an early abort rule for oversized batches.
Carmen: Draft route config snippet for the canary:
```
route: harborcrest-hybrid-quant
- match: customer_id == "harborcrest"
- dynamic_rules:
  - if prompt_length < 140 and request_type == "completion": model=redwood/compact-mid:int8
  - else: model=redwood/prime-v1
- canary: {model: redwood/compact-mid:int8, weight: 10}
- hosted_fallback_pct: 15
- autoscale_headroom: 0.25
- continuous_batch_size_limit: 44
- kv_prefetch_ttl_s: 75
- session_pin_streaming: true
- rollback: {p95_delta_ms: 180, error_rate_pct: 0.5}
```
Noah: Add a semantic fingerprint gate: compute embedding-similarity between baseline and canary outputs on a 15-sample customer template set. Require mean cosine >= 0.987 and no more than 1 human-fail in a light QA pass before stepping beyond 10%. Also capture Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for streaming sessions and require no >4% increase.
Hector (HarborCrest): We need exact phrasing on our public summaries. The semantic gate is essential. Also prefer a 1-hour shadow run (A/B logging only) before any live canary so we can confirm no regressions in our templates.
Priya: Agreed. Plan: 1) run 1h shadowed A/B capture (no user change) with the compact-mid:int8 path, 2) run automated diffs (BLEU/ROUGE + embedding-sim) on 15 templates, 3) one QA reviewer spot-check 15 samples. If shadow run passes, start 10% canary for 2h, then step to 40% if stable. Rollback triggers: p95 > baseline + 180ms for 10m OR error_rate > 0.5% OR semantic_cosine_mean < 0.987 OR human_failures >=1.
Carmen: ops-bot, please schedule the shadow run and canary, create alerts for harborcrest-p95, harborcrest-ttft, harborcrest-semantic-cosine, and configure auto-revert policy as above.
ops-bot: Shadow run scheduled: harborcrest-shadow-4991234567; Canary job created: harborcrest-canary-4991234567; Monitors: p95_tokens, error_rate, ttft_streaming, semantic_cosine_mean. Auto-revert rules set: p95_delta_ms=180, error_rate_pct=0.5, semantic_cosine_threshold=0.987, human_failures_threshold=1.
Noah: I'll pre-provision +1 GPU to the dedicated pool for the first 3 hours of the shadow+canary window and enable adaptive kernel selection for the int8 path. Also turning on difflogging to capture token-level edits for QA (retain 7d).
Hector (HarborCrest): Thanks 1. Please include our QA and legal on the shadow A/B capture. If the metrics and QA look good we are open to a phased migration to the compact path to reduce costs.
Carmen: Action items: Carmen prepare 15-template eval set + invite QA/legal, Priya & Noah implement shadow routing + pool limits + pre-warm, ops-bot run shadow + canary and handle auto-reverts. I'll post interim metrics here after the 1h shadow and after the first 30m of canary. :white_check_mark:
